title: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for Recursive Self-Improvement
abstract: arXiv:2608.20318v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) asks whether an AI system can improve the process that produces AI systems, so that the next system inherits the improvement. That process is the training algorithm: a better objective or update rule improves the compute\mbox{-}capability exchange rate for every subsequent run, including the one that produces the next agent. Whether RSI is feasible therefore turns on whether an agent can design training algorithms. No benchmark isolates that ability: existing suites are won by collecting data or by tuning hyperparameters, and none tells a change to how a run is executed apart from a change to how the model learns. We present AI4AI\mbox{-}Bench, 10 frozen research repositories spanning 10 training algorithm families. In each task, an agent has 4 hours on one B300 to rewrite the training algorithm; its code is then rerun from scratch for up to 12 hours and scored by a fixed evaluator hidden from the agent,

translated_title: AI4AI-Bench：面向递归自我改进的算法设计中LLM代理的基准测试
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.20318v1 公告类型：新 摘要：递归自我改进（RSI）探讨的是AI系统能否改进生成AI系统的过程，从而让下一代系统继承这种改进。该过程即训练算法：一个更好的目标函数或更新规则能提高每次后续运行（包括生成下一代代理的那次）的计算-能力交换率。因此，RSI是否可行取决于代理能否设计训练算法。现有基准测试并未孤立地评估这一能力：现有套件通过收集数据或调整超参数来取胜，且没有区分对运行方式的改变与对模型学习方式的改变。我们提出AI4AI-Bench，包含10个覆盖10种训练算法家族的冻结研究仓库。在每个任务中，代理有4小时在一台B300上重写训练算法；其代码随后从头重新运行最多12小时，并由一个对代理隐藏的固定评估器评分。
tldr: 本文提出AI4AI-Bench，这是一个首个专门用于评估LLM代理设计训练算法能力的基准测试，通过10个冻结研究仓库和固定评估器来测试递归自我改进的可行性。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces AI4AI-Bench, the first benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLM agents' ability to design training algorithms, testing the feasibility of recursive self-improvement through 10 frozen research repositories and a fixed evaluator.
